newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's chemical plant boosts Jan-Aug profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's chemical plant boosts Jan-Aug profit.

text.p: Bulgaria's chemical plant Himko, one of the country's biggest firms earmarked for sell-offs, has boosted its profits in recent years, earning some three billion levs net profit for the first eight months of the year.
Himko, located in the town of Vratza north of Sofia, had a net profit of 906.3 million levs for the first eight months last year, while the plant's net profit for the whole 1994 was 60 million levs.

"Some of the reasons for the plant's profitable operations are the improved management and investment and the upgrading of the installations," Himko's spokeswoman Silvia Nakova told Reuters by telephone.
Officials said $45 million had been invested this year for upgrading the plant's installations. The plant has 20 installations including seven carbamide and four reforming ones.
Apart from carbamide, the list of Himko's products includes urea, ammonia, sulphur-containing products, industrial gases, catalysts, pigments and fertilizers.
Earlier this year Himko established a joint venture with Frankfurt-based Messer Grieshelm GmbH, a subsidiary of German chemical giant Hoechst.
The venture is aimed at the distribution, marketing and sales of industrial gases in neighbouring states.
Officials said there were plans for the establishment of a new joint venture for marketing and distribution in Turkey called Himko Turkey. They did not elaborate.
"Himko's goals are to develop and enlarge the market of its products as currently some 90 percent of its production is exported," Nakova said.
